name: PIK3CA-related overgrowth syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and molecular diagnostic criteria for PIK3CA-related overgrowth syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of a somatic activating mutation in the PIK3CA gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
Asymmetric segmental overgrowth of soft tissue and/or bone affecting one or more body regions
Presence of vascular malformations such as capillary, venous, or lymphatic anomalies in affected regions
Exclusion of other genetic overgrowth syndromes such as Proteus syndrome or Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of a somatic PIK3CA mutation plus clinical evidence of segmental overgrowth
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular confirmation is essential due to phenotypic overlap with other overgrowth syndromes.

laboratory: Detection of somatic activating mutations in PIK3CA gene via next-generation sequencing
Normal routine blood counts unless secondary complications
imaging: MRI showing asymmetric soft tissue and bone hypertrophy
CT or MRI angiography for detailed vascular mapping
other: Histopathology of affected tissue showing cellular hypertrophy without malignancy
Clinical exclusion of other overgrowth syndromes

distinguishingFeatures: AKT1 gene mutation instead of PIK3CA
Progressive asymmetric overgrowth with cerebriform connective tissue nevi
Capillary malformations (port-wine stains) present at birth
Venous and lymphatic malformations with limb hypertrophy
No confirmed PIK3CA mutation in all cases

redFlags: Rapid progression of overgrowth causing functional impairment
Development of deep venous thrombosis or pulmonary embolism
Neurological deterioration including seizures or developmental delay
references: Keppler-Noreuil KM, Rios JJ, Parker VE, et al. PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum (PROS): diagnostic and testing eligibility criteria, differential diagnosis, and evaluation. Am J Med Genet A. 2015;167A(2):287-295.
Lindhurst MJ, Sapp JC, Teer JK, et al. A mosaic activating mutation in AKT1 associated with the Proteus syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2011;365(7):611-619.

Mirzaa GM, Campbell CD, Solovieff N, et al. Association of MTOR mutations with developmental brain disorders, including megalencephaly, focal cortical dysplasia, and epilepsy. JAMA Neurol. 2016;73(7):836-845.
